title: A lead change adds one history entry and none for the lines it moves
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has both).
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  3. In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.
  4. At least 3 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Ralph Edwards", "Dana Ortiz"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Dana Ortiz") and an email.
    • Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
  5. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
  6. Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
    • On the Lines tab click New Line, enter a name (e.g. "Brake inspection") and labor hours (e.g. 2.0), and save the line.
    • Click the line's Approve (check) button so the work order status reads Approved.
    • Add a second line (e.g. "Oil change") with no technician before setting the lead, so both lines follow Esther Howard.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; in the design its button tooltip reads "Board").
  2. Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
  3. Note the time, then drag the card from Esther Howard's column into Ralph Edwards' column.
  4. If a "Clear …'s scheduled shifts?" prompt opens, click Keep shifts.
  5. Open the work order and open its change history (audit log). Write down where you found it.
  6. Count the entries added by this change.
  7. On the Lines tab click the first line's name to open the Edit Line dialog and set Technicians to "Dana Ortiz", then save.
  8. Open the change history again and read the newest entries.
  9. Repeat steps 3 to 6 using More actions > Reassign lead technician (Ralph Edwards → Esther Howard), then once more by changing Lead Technician on the work order page (Esther Howard → Ralph Edwards).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Each lead change (drag, Reassign dialog, work order page) adds exactly one entry showing the previous lead, the new lead, your user as the person who made it, and the time (e.g. Esther Howard → Ralph Edwards, by you, at the time you noted).
  • No separate entries appear for the two lines that moved with the lead (3 lead changes = 3 entries, not 9).
  • Changing a line's technician directly in Edit Line still adds its own line entry, as it does today.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R9, S4-R17, S4-R18, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions FF-4 history (audit actor is the logged-in user). Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R9: “Every lead-change path records one audit entry with the previous lead, new lead, logged-in actor, and time.”
  • S4-R17: “Do not create separate audit entries for implicit line movements caused by a lead change.”
  • S4-R18: “Continue existing line auditing for technician changes made directly on a work order line.”
